questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves while riding?

options.text: Make it difficult to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If possible, change lanes to let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What is allowed in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones prohibit all passing. You cannot pass by riding off the main roadway either.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright colors, keep your headlight on at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required for a street-legal motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: A windshield wiper
questions.explanation: Street-legal motorcycles must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.

questions.question: How often should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent safety problems. Small issues can be more serious on a motorcycle than a car.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates all reduce tire grip. Dry concrete provides good traction.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: Their effects are stronger than when used alone.
They are less dangerous than when used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects are stronger than when used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can reduce your riding ability. Combining drugs with alcohol makes the danger even greater.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material to protect your hands.

questions.question: The proper body position on a motorcycle is:

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the handle grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the handle grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the handle grips. This position lets you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: Which footwear is best for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles give the best protection. Laced boots are best. If your laces are long, tuck them away before riding.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle approaches too quickly from behind.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oily areas, and metal plates are all slippery. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is NOT a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-compliant helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but be loose enough to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be performed by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means:

options.text: Within minutes of being consumed, alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
Alcohol never gets removed from the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Once in your system, your body gets rid of alcohol quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of being consumed, alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Because it does not need to be digested, alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. The body eliminates about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Night riding is usually:

options.text: Easier than day riding because you can see other vehicle lights better.
Harder than day riding because visibility is poor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than day riding because visibility is poor.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well and other drivers cannot see you as easily. Without natural light and shadows, it is difficult to judge distances.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is good to drag your feet.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as this may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can use them quickly if needed.

questions.question: When it is clear that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need to signal at stop lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if it seems obvious. Other vehicles may be near you but out of sight. Signaling is always required.

questions.question: A simple way to make a motorcycle more visible is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to make your motorcycle visible is to keep your headlight on at all times while riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, wear a jacket:

options.text: No matter what the weather is.
Only if the ride is longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what the weather is.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from injury, sun exposure, and dehydration.
